summary:
BEYOND MED is an AI-powered astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support the assessment of astronaut health during long-duration space missions. We developed a software platform that combines physiological signal acquisition, machine learning, and a web-based interface to identify deviations from normal health-related patterns. Using Electrooculography (EOG) signals acquired through the BioAmp EXG Pill, our system applies a One-Class Support Vector Machine (One-Class SVM) trained on normal EOG data to identify unusual signal patterns without requiring extensive labeled abnormal-condition datasets.

BEYOND MED addresses the challenge of maintaining astronaut health during space exploration, where limited medical resources and delayed communication with Earth make continuous health assessment particularly important. By exploring automated anomaly detection and accessible monitoring, the project aims to support early identification of potential physiological irregularities. Our long-term vision is to contribute to safer human spaceflight and more sustainable missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
BEYOND MED – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

Project Overview

BEYOND MED is a software-based astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support continuous assessment of astronaut health during space missions. It aims to help identify potential physiological and behavioral abnormalities by analyzing health-related signals and detecting deviations from an individual's normal baseline.

How It Works

BEYOND MED processes physiological data and applies machine-learning-based anomaly detection to identify patterns that deviate from normal conditions. One of its key components uses Electrooculography (EOG) data to analyze eye-movement signals. A One-Class Support Vector Machine (One-Class SVM) model is trained using normal EOG feature data to establish a baseline of expected patterns. Incoming data can then be evaluated against this baseline to identify unusual signal patterns.

The software presents the analyzed information through a web-based interface, allowing users to interpret monitoring results and understand potential deviations. The system is designed as a health-monitoring and decision-support concept rather than a diagnostic medical device.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Early anomaly identification: Helps identify unusual physiological signal patterns that may warrant further investigation.
  • Continuous monitoring potential: Supports repeated assessment of astronaut health throughout space missions.
  • Machine-learning integration: Uses anomaly detection to identify deviations without requiring a large collection of labeled abnormal-condition datasets.
  • Mission health awareness: Could help astronauts and mission-support teams become more aware of potential health-related changes.
  • Future adaptability: Provides a foundation for expanding astronaut health-monitoring capabilities for long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.

The intended impact is to contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration by exploring accessible, software-driven approaches to astronaut health monitoring.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies

The project was developed using a combination of software development and machine-learning technologies:

  • Python: Data processing and machine-learning implementation.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Numerical data manipulation and feature processing.
  • Scikit-learn: Implementation of the One-Class SVM anomaly-detection model and StandardScaler.
  • ONNX: Model-export format for potential cross-platform deployment.
  • React.js: Development of the web-based user interface.
  • Arduino IDE: Development and testing of the EOG signal acquisition hardware.
  • BioAmp EXG Pill: EOG signal acquisition hardware used for physiological signal experimentation.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of BEYOND MED lies in exploring how machine-learning-based anomaly detection can be applied to astronaut health monitoring. Instead of relying exclusively on predefined thresholds, the One-Class SVM approach learns patterns from normal EOG data and identifies deviations from those patterns.

This approach is particularly interesting for space missions, where collecting labeled examples of every possible abnormal physiological condition may be difficult. Combining physiological signal acquisition, machine learning, and a web-based monitoring interface creates an approach that can be developed further for future space-health applications.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several factors while designing BEYOND MED:

  1. Space mission constraints: Health-monitoring approaches should be suitable for environments with limited resources and demanding operational conditions.
  2. Data availability: The machine-learning approach should work with available normal physiological data without depending on extensive abnormal-condition datasets.
  3. Computational efficiency: The model should be practical to execute on resource-constrained computing platforms.
  4. Signal reliability: Physiological signals can contain noise and artifacts, making appropriate signal processing important.
  5. Usability: Health information should be presented through an understandable interface.
  6. Scalability: The software architecture should provide opportunities for future development and integration into broader astronaut health-monitoring systems.

Conclusion

BEYOND MED explores the intersection of biomedical signal processing, machine learning, and human space exploration. By developing a system that analyzes physiological signals and identifies deviations from normal patterns, our project aims to contribute to the future of intelligent astronaut health monitoring, particularly for long-duration lunar and interplanetary missions.
